summary:
Iter19 — 'Objects are not valid as a React child' crash retest. VERDICT: PASS. All 4 defensive layers land correctly and the root-cause crash is eliminated.

LAYER 1 (utils/errors.ts) — VERIFIED by inspection. `safeStr` handles null/undefined/string/number/boolean/bigint/array/{msg}/{message}/{detail}/{error}/{description}, falls back to JSON.stringify, and never throws. `errText` walks e.response.data.detail → data.message → e.message → stringified e → fallback. All branches are string-safe.

LAYER 2 (Toast.tsx) — VERIFIED. `show()` signature widened to `(type: ToastType, message: any)`; body coerces incoming value via `safeStr(message, 'Something went wrong')` BEFORE calling setToast. safeStr import present (line 7). The <Text> at line 63 renders `toast.message` which is now guaranteed to be a string.

LAYER 3 (kycGate.ts interceptor) — VERIFIED via curl+Playwright. Backend still returns detail as OBJECT with code='KYC_REQUIRED'. Interceptor now: (a) emits KYC_REQUIRED event when status===403 and detail is object with code==='KYC_REQUIRED'; (b) unconditionally normalizes data.detail — if object → prefers d.message, then d.msg, then joined validation msg[] array, else JSON.stringify; (c) preserves the original object under data.detailRaw for advanced consumers. The try/catch around the normalization block guarantees it can never itself throw.

LAYER 4 (safe render at Text sites) — VERIFIED. /app/frontend/app/kyc/index.tsx:74 wraps `{safeStr(err)}` inside <Text>. /app/frontend/app/(auth)/forgot-password.tsx:142 wraps `{safeStr(err)}`. Both files also import errText for their catch blocks (setErr(errText(e, ...))).

BACKEND RAW CONTRACT — VERIFIED. POST /api/forex/positions with a fresh signup user (kyc_status='pending', kyc_profile.status='not_started') returns EXACTLY: status 403, body {detail:{code:'KYC_REQUIRED', message:'KYC verification required before using this service.', current_status:'not_started', action_url:'/kyc', completion_required:true}}. This is the raw pre-interceptor shape that all four layers defend against. Verified via pytest (backend/tests/test_kyc_gate_iter19.py — 3/3 pass) and via direct fetch inside the running app tab.

END-TO-END BROWSER RUN — signup fresh non-KYC user → seed token → navigate /forex/symbol/XAUUSD → tap SELL chip → tap 'SELL 0.1 XAU/USD' confirm. Result: zero page errors (page.on 'pageerror' fired 0 times), zero occurrences of the substring 'Objects are not valid as a React child' in console output, zero white screens, zero ErrorBoundary triggers. The XAU/USD trade ticket renders cleanly with BID/ASK/SELL/BUY, lot size selector (0.01/0.1/1/5/10), TP/SL fields, margin, and confirm button. The two 401 console errors observed are from /api/forex/balance and /api/ai/profile calls made before the Zustand auth store hydrates from localStorage — this is a pre-existing benign symptom (not caused by this fix) and does NOT surface any Object-as-child crash.

REGRESSION — demo@mfb.in / demo1234 still logs in (POST /api/auth/login → 200 token) and hitting POST /api/forex/positions with SELL 0.01 lot is NOT gated by KYC (test 3/3 pass).

CONSOLE HYGIENE — During the full non-KYC forex flow, page.on('console','error') fired exactly 2 times, both '401 Failed to load resource' for pre-hydration API calls. Substring 'Objects are not valid as a React child' MUST NOT appear — CONFIRMED 0 occurrences across all navigations.

Not caused by this iteration; consider adding a `useAuthStore.persist.rehydrate()` await before firing effect API calls on protected routes.
critical_code_review_comments: GOOD — kycGate.ts interceptor uses a defensive try/catch around the entire normalization block (line 46-62), so a malformed response.data can never itself throw and take down the interceptor chain.

GOOD — kycGate.ts preserves the original object under data.detailRaw before overwriting data.detail — the KycRequiredModal / any advanced consumer can still read the structured payload from detailRaw. This is a solid non-destructive normalization pattern.

GOOD — utils/errors.ts safeStr handles the exact FastAPI validation array shape [{msg,type,loc}] via the recursive `Array.isArray(x)` branch which delegates back to safeStr on each item — matches the interceptor's array-handling path.

GOOD — Toast.tsx widens `show(type: ToastType, message: any)` — this is intentional: it accepts any type from callers that may still pass a raw error or object during the transition period, and always coerces safely.
NIT — errText() falls through to `String(e)` at the end which for a plain object returns '[object Object]'; the code correctly filters that out and returns the fallback instead. Solid.

NIT — The interceptor's fallback JSON.stringify(d) branch will surface a raw JSON blob in the Toast if the object has no message/msg/detail/error/description key AND is not an array. Rare, but users would see something like '{"code":"X","foo":1}'. Acceptable — better than a crash — and only fires for truly unstructured backend errors.

rca_of_issue: Original crash — RCA: FastAPI KYC gate returns HTTPException(403, {code, message, current_status, ...}) which serializes as {'detail': <object>} in the response body. Frontend catch handlers across the app did `show('error', e?.response?.data?.detail || e?.message || '...')` which passed the raw object into <Text>{obj}</Text> → React throws 'Objects are not valid as a React child'. FIX (4 layers): (1) utils/errors.ts safeStr/errText coerce any value to a string; (2) Toast.show() defensively re-coerces its message arg via safeStr — belt-and-suspenders even if a caller forgets errText(); (3) kycGate axios interceptor rewrites response.data.detail from object → string (prefers .message > .msg > joined validation-array-msgs > JSON.stringify) and preserves the original at response.data.detailRaw so KycRequiredModal can still fire on the correct code+action_url; (4) explicit safeStr wraps at the two known Text render sites that used raw {err}. REPRODUCTION (pre-fix): sign up a fresh user, do NOT complete KYC, tap SELL on /forex/symbol/XAUUSD, confirm order → axios throws → catch does show('error', e.response.data.detail) → passes {code,message,...} into <Text> → ErrorBoundary catches 'Objects are not valid as a React child'. VERIFICATION (post-fix): same reproduction path now produces zero React errors; the interceptor rewrites detail to the message string BEFORE the catch handler sees it; even if any handler somehow bypassed the interceptor, Toast.show() and the explicit safeStr() wraps would still absorb the object. MITIGATION IS COMPLETE.
